summary: GRAPHITE-D27: every provider call now has a hard total wall-clock deadline. Twice on 2026-10-02 a live Graphite triage call sat with no response for 26 minutes or more, its operation still RESERVED, because model_provider passed timeout_seconds to urllib, which bounds each socket operation (connect, proxy CONNECT, TLS handshake, each read) and never the whole call; a reply arriving in pieces, each inside the timeout, kept it open. The exchange now runs in a daemon worker joined for timeout_seconds plus a named 10 s margin (130 s for triage); past it the call's TCP and TLS sockets are shut and ProviderDeadlineExceeded is raised, which classifies as UNKNOWN: the full reservation stays, nothing is settled or resent, triage stops RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED and the GRAPHITE-D17 write-off handles it at the next start. It applies to every adapter, since they share one transport; calls inside the deadline are unchanged. Tests use a local HTTPS server that stalls, trickles one byte at a time or never speaks, plus a mutation check. Nothing here grades, qualifies or rewards.
